title: Predicting activation-barrier and plasticity-onset statistics in a model of glasses
authors: Makoto Suda, Edan Lerner, Eran Bouchbinder
abstract: A recently introduced anharmonic mean-field model unifiedly reproduced a broad range of low-temperature glass phenomena --- including harmonic nonphononic spectral properties, linear micromechanics and strongly driven elasto-plastic dynamics --- indicating that its underlying energy landscape is intrinsically glassy. Here, we apply a nonlinear modes framework to the model and derive analytic predictions for the asymptotic distributions of activation barriers $p(Δ{U})\!\sim\!(Δ{U})^{1/4}$ and the external force needed for the onset of plasticity $p(f_{\rm c})\sim f_{\rm c}^{2/3}$, for their extreme-value scaling and for $\langleΔ{U}\rangle$ beyond the asymptotic regime. These predictions are expected to equally apply to the mean-field model and to finite-dimensional glasses. We develop efficient algorithms for sampling minima and saddles of the model's glassy potential energy landscape, and quantitatively confirm the theoretical predictions. This progress is enabled by identifying a subset of collective degrees of freedom that are physically relevant for activated glassy dynamics, which like the theoretical predictions should apply to realistic glasses.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework using nonlinear modes to analyze the energy landscape of a mean-field model for glasses. It derives universal scaling laws for the statistics of activation barriers and plasticity-onset forces. The results provide quantitative predictions for glassy dynamics that are expected to hold for real amorphous solids.
main_problem: The paper aims to predict the statistical distributions of activation barriers ($\Delta U$) and the critical external force ($f_c$) required to induce plasticity in a model of amorphous solids (glasses).
main_result: The authors derive asymptotic scaling laws, predicting $p(\Delta U_c) \sim (\Delta U_c)^{1/4}$ and $p(f_c) \sim f_c^{2/3}$, and confirm these predictions using specialized sampling algorithms.
method: The analysis employs a nonlinear modes framework applied to an anharmonic mean-field Hamiltonian, focusing on 'cubic modes' to characterize the energy landscape's soft directions.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by an anharmonic mean-field Hamiltonian for continuous degrees of freedom, incorporating random quadratic stiffnesses and disordered Gaussian couplings, characteristic of glassy materials.
key_observables: Activation barriers ($\Delta U$), plasticity onset force ($f_c$), and the frequency distribution ($ho(\omega_\pi)$) of the softest vibrational modes.
important_parameters: The shape parameter $\eta = b_2^3/(b_2 b_4)$ is crucial, with physical relevance restricted to $\eta < 3$. System size $N$ dictates the scaling of mean values ($\langle\Delta Uangle \sim N^{-4/5}$).
main_assumptions: The predictions are assumed to apply universally to both the mean-field model and realistic, finite-dimensional glasses.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the parameter space of cubic modes ($\eta$ vs. $b_2^3 - b_2 b_4$). Figure 2 confirms the universal quartic tail ($ho(\omega_\pi) \sim \omega_\pi^4$) in the frequency spectrum. Figure 3 shows numerical confirmation of plastic instability detection.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the anharmonic mean-field model and the nonlinear modes framework. It then analyzes the relevant parameter regimes ($\eta < 3$) and derives the asymptotic scaling laws for $\Delta U$ and $f_c$. Finally, it develops and uses efficient algorithms to sample the potential energy landscape to quantitatively confirm these theoretical predictions.
why_interesting: The work provides concrete, analytically derived scaling laws for non-equilibrium phenomena (plasticity, activated dynamics) in disordered systems, which are highly relevant to understanding energy dissipation and structural failure in complex materials.
